skill.name: security-scanning-security-dependencies
skill.description: Analyze dependency manifests and lockfiles for known vulnerabilities, license issues, SBOM needs, and remediation priorities across major ecosystems.
skill.summary: Scan dependencies, prioritize vulnerabilities, and plan SBOM-based remediation.

security_audit.summary: The static command and filesystem alerts are mostly safe examples for dependency scanning, not hidden executable behavior. No prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or malicious network intent was found. The main residual risk is the automated update workflow, which can modify dependencies and should require explicit approval and testing.

remediation.issue: Automated update commands can modify dependency manifests and lockfiles.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval before running update or fix commands, and run tests after every dependency change.

remediation.issue: Scanner examples depend on external package manager tools.
remediation.suggestion: Document required tools, expected network behavior, and trusted project directory assumptions before command execution.

content.value_statement: Dependency vulnerabilities and license risks are difficult to track across ecosystems. This skill guides scanning, prioritization, SBOM creation, and remediation planning.
actual_capabilities: Detects npm, Python, Go, and Rust dependency manifests and lockfiles.
Guides vulnerability scanning with npm audit, Safety, govulncheck, and cargo audit.
Prioritizes findings by severity, fix availability, and exploit context.
Shows how to generate CycloneDX-style SBOM and SARIF report structures.
Provides CI workflow patterns for scheduled dependency security checks.
Outlines remediation planning for critical and high severity packages.
limitations: Requires local scanner tools and package managers to be installed.
Results depend on public vulnerability databases and their freshness.
Automated update examples can change dependencies and need approval.
Does not replace manual review for breaking changes or license decisions.

use_cases.title: Audit Release Dependencies
use_cases.description: Scan dependency files before a release and identify critical fixes that must block deployment.

use_cases.title: Prepare Compliance Evidence
use_cases.description: Generate SBOM-oriented inventory notes and summarize vulnerable packages for compliance review.

use_cases.title: Standardize Repository Checks
use_cases.description: Create repeatable CI dependency scanning steps for teams using several package ecosystems.

prompt_templates.title: Scan One Project
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner scan of a local repository.
prompt_templates.prompt: Scan this project for dependency vulnerabilities. Identify the package ecosystems, required tools, and the highest priority remediation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Review Lockfiles
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of manifests and lockfiles.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the dependency manifests and lockfiles in this repository. Summarize vulnerable packages, fixed versions, and test steps before changes.

prompt_templates.title: Plan CI Scanning
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a dependency security scanning workflow for this repository. Include scan cadence, failure thresholds, artifacts, and ownership guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize Remediation Program
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze dependency risk across ecosystems and create a remediation plan using severity, exploitability, fix availability, release impact, and SBOM needs.

output_examples.input: A Node.js service has package files and a request to assess release readiness.
output_examples.output: The report identifies npm as the ecosystem, lists critical and high issues first, names fixed versions, and recommends blocking release until tests pass.

output_examples.input: A mixed Python and Go repository needs scheduled security checks.
output_examples.output: The workflow recommendation includes separate scanner steps, saved artifacts, threshold rules for critical findings, and an owner for remediation review.

output_examples.input: A compliance team requests supply chain evidence for an application.
output_examples.output: The response summarizes SBOM coverage, vulnerable components, unresolved license questions, and follow-up actions for audit evidence.

best_practices: Run scans on a regular schedule and before high-risk releases.
Prioritize fixes using severity, exploit availability, and application exposure.
Test every dependency update before merging remediation changes.
anti_patterns: Running auto-fix commands without explicit approval and review.
Treating scanner output as complete without checking false positives.
Ignoring lockfiles when assessing actual deployed dependency versions.

faq.question: What ecosystems does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers npm, Python, Go, and Rust examples, with patterns that can be adapted to other package managers.

faq.question: Can it generate an SBOM?
faq.answer: It provides guidance for SBOM-style component inventory and CycloneDX-oriented reporting, but output depends on available project data.

faq.question: Does it automatically fix vulnerabilities?
faq.answer: It includes remediation examples, but dependency changes should run only after explicit approval and testing.

faq.question: Does it need network access?
faq.answer: Many scanners query vulnerability databases or package registries, so network access may be required for current results.

faq.question: Can it evaluate license risk?
faq.answer: It can guide license review and flag packages for follow-up, but legal decisions need qualified review.

faq.question: Is it suitable for CI pipelines?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes CI scanning patterns, thresholds, saved artifacts, and scheduled scan guidance.
